title: How to Get Startup Ideas: live in the future, notice what's missing, build what's interesting
summary: Paul Graham argues you shouldn't try to think up startup ideas. Become someone at the leading edge of a fast-changing field and notice problems, ideally ones you have yourself. Good ideas are narrow, deep "wells" that a small group wants badly. Ignore the schlep and unsexy filters, and worry about users rather than competitors.

principles.text: Don't brainstorm startup ideas; look for problems, preferably your own.
principles.quote: The way to get startup ideas is not to try to think of startup ideas. It's to look for problems, preferably problems you have yourself.

principles.text: Build a narrow, deep well: a small group wanting it badly beats a broad group mildly interested.
principles.quote: you can either build something a large number of people want a small amount, or something a small number of people want a large amount. Choose the latter.

principles.text: Test an idea by asking who wants it right now, even as a crappy v1 from unknown founders.
principles.quote: Who wants this so much that they'll use it even when it's a crappy version one made by a two-person startup they've never heard of? If you can't answer that, the idea is probably bad.

principles.text: Live in the future and build what's missing; notice ideas rather than think them up.
principles.quote: The verb you want to be using with respect to startup ideas is not "think up" but "notice."

principles.text: Turn off the schlep and unsexy filters; tedious problems hold valuable, uncrowded ideas.
principles.quote: If you let your mind wander a few blocks down the street to the messy, tedious ideas, you'll find valuable ones just sitting there waiting to be implemented.

principles.text: Focus on users, not competitors; a crowded market signals demand if you see what others overlook.
principles.quote: Err on the side of doing things where you'll face competitors. Inexperienced founders usually give competitors more credit than they deserve.
